description: A single .NET global tool that drives C# services on AWS — bootstrap, deploy, and rollback for Lambda, ECS Fargate, static-site, and coupled full-stack targets, all from one committed manifest.
releaseNotes:
- A rejected library wave can be seen and its intent restored (proposal 0059 P1).
  A release commit deletes the declarations it resolved before anything is published. When its release execution was then rejected at Approval, the versions were on no feed, the intent was gone from the tree, and the only way to learn why was the AWS console.
  - `kanject packages intent restore --from <release commit>` writes back, byte for byte, the declarations that commit consumed, read from its parent. You commit them and run `packages release` again. It refuses with the new `KANCLI795`, writing nothing, when the commit is not a release commit on the tracked branch, when a version it set is already published, when its execution failed at Publish (retry that stage instead), or when a file of the same name exists with different content.
  - `packages release status` says how an execution ended. A rejection, a stop and a supersession are still `Failed` in `pipeline.state`, and the report adds which (`pipeline.ending`), who and when, the approver's summary, and whether the failed stage can still be retried. The person is shown by session or user name, never the full ARN.
  - `packages release status` works on a pipeline with no rehearsal. With `rehearsal.enabled: false` in `packaging/release.pipeline.json` the stack no longer needs a rehearsal project, and the report goes by the pipeline execution. It failed `KANCLI556` before.
  - A commit pushed underneath a later one is found. Status reports the execution that carried it and names the commit that execution ran, instead of "not started". The search through the pipeline's history now stops at executions older than the commit.
  - `packages release status --pending` lists every version the checkout holds that no feed has and a release commit on the tracked branch set, with that commit and where its execution stands. It reads the full package surface and changes nothing.
  - Release commits carry a `Kanject-Release-Wave: <part>` trailer, which is how a version a release commit set is told from a manual edit. Release commits written before it are recognised by their shape. `packages release` itself accepts and refuses exactly what it did before.

- `packages release` refuses to author on top of an unpublished release commit (proposal 0059 P2).
  A release commit whose execution failed or was rejected stays on the tracked branch with versions no feed has. The next run resolved a different part and stopped with `KANCLI545` ("remove the manual version edit"), though nobody had edited anything. The front door now recognises the state while it plans, and refuses before it branches or commits.
  - `KANCLI793`: the earlier release commit's execution is still running or awaiting approval. Approve it, or reject it and restore. From the tracked branch's own tip the run stops as "already promoted" and names the execution.
  - `KANCLI794`: the execution failed, was rejected or was stopped, and the declarations the commit consumed are not back. The message names who rejected it and when, the remedy (`packages intent restore --from <commit>`), and `git revert <commit>` to drop the change. After a failed Publish only the retry is offered. With the declarations back the run carries on and ships the versions; if it resolves a higher part it names the revert instead.
  - `KANCLI796`: the pipeline cannot be read, no execution carries the commit, or the clone is shallow. `--accept-unknown-standing <commit>` carries on when the execution can never be read again; it must name the printed commit, is recorded in the release commit, and still requires the consumed declarations to be back.
  - The cost is in the rare case only. The check uses the feed listing the plan already makes, and reads the pipeline only when a version is pending. `--no-push` reads the pipeline then too.
  - A rerun keeps its release commit's intent. A rerun of `packages release` on a minor or major release commit that is not on the tracked branch yet resolved `patch`, because the commit had consumed its declarations, and failed `KANCLI545` against its own versions. It now takes the part and notes from that commit's `release.intent.json`, also when a fix was committed on top of it after a failed rehearsal.
  - `packages bump plan` names the release commit. Run directly on a full clone, its `KANCLI545` says which release commit set an unpublished version and how to restore or revert it. With no git history, or a shallow one, the message is unchanged.
